bull.b: Strong DTC growth shows increasing consumer demand and gives On greater control over pricing, customer relationships, and product presentation. A rising DTC mix can support durable revenue quality and margins while reducing reliance on third-party retail partners over the next several quarters.

The combination of a 65.4% gross margin and nearly 20% adjusted EBITDA margin indicates that On is scaling profitably while retaining premium brand economics. Management’s full-year margin targets suggest profitability is expected to remain structurally strong rather than depend solely on volume growth.

bull.t: Strong balance sheet and cash generation
bull.b: A net cash position above CHF 1.2 billion provides substantial financial flexibility to fund product innovation, retail expansion, and international growth without relying heavily on additional borrowing. Together with recent cash generation, this strengthens resilience and supports long-term strategic investment.

bear.b: Slower wholesale growth, especially in the Americas, indicates that demand and sell-through are less consistent in multi-brand retail than in On’s DTC channel. Continued weakness could constrain distribution-led expansion and make revenue growth more dependent on the company’s own stores and digital platforms.

A 30% inventory increase alongside promotional wholesale conditions raises the risk that product may require additional markdowns or take longer to sell through. Even if volume growth is the main driver, sustained inventory expansion could pressure working capital, margins, and operating cash conversion.

Higher U.S. import tariffs create an ongoing cost headwind for products sold into an important market, potentially pressuring gross margins or requiring pricing actions. The uncertain timing of refunds adds variability to reported profitability and cash benefits over the coming quarters.
